questions.stem: A biogas digester produces $200\,\text{m}^3/\text{day}$ of biogas with $60\%$ methane. The methane energy content at $35.8\,\text{MJ/m}^3$ is _____ MJ/day.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Energy = biogas × CH₄ fraction × energy density.

**Working.**
$$200\times0.6\times35.8=4296.$$

**Answer.** $4296\,\text{MJ/day}$

questions.stem: A biogas plant produces $500\,\text{m}^3/\text{day}$ biogas with $65\%$ methane. After upgrading to $97\%$ biomethane, the daily biomethane output is _____ m³.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Biomethane = biogas × CH₄ fraction × upgrading efficiency.

**Working.**
$$500\times0.65\times(0.97/0.65)=500\times0.67=335.$$
Wait: raw CH₄ = 325 m³; after upgrading to 97% purity, output = 325/0.97 = 335.

**Answer.** $335\,\text{m}^3/\text{day}$

questions.subject: Solid & Hazardous Waste Management
questions.stem: Which of the following are advantages of bioremediation over physical/chemical methods?
options: applicable to a wide range of organic contaminants
complete mineralisation to CO₂ and water is always guaranteed
low energy consumption compared to thermal methods
effective under all soil and groundwater conditions
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Bioremediation is cost-effective for organics in-situ with low energy, but performance depends on site conditions and is not guaranteed to achieve complete mineralisation.

**Answer.** In-situ treatment avoids excavation costs, applicable to a wide range of organic contaminants, low energy consumption compared to thermal methods
